resources.string: The agent sees host aliases only, never passwords or keys.
Hosts and credentials aren\'t included in backups.
The agent refers to this host by its ID. Start with a lowercase letter; digits, _ and - allowed; up to 48 characters. Leave empty to generate one from the hostname.
Choose an OpenSSH private key file, or copy the whole key and paste it from the clipboard.
Private key loaded in memory. Save to store it securely on this device.
Generate key, save and copy public key
After saving, add the public key to the server\'s authorized_keys.
Leave credential fields empty to keep the saved credential. Import or generate a key to replace it.
The presented host fingerprint matches the saved fingerprint.
Check this fingerprint against the server. A changed fingerprint may mean a different server.
Delete %1$s and its saved credential from this device?
The agent is configuring %1$s. The password is kept in this device\'s secure storage and is never sent to the AI.
The agent wants to connect to %1$s (%2$s).
Agents can only connect to configured hosts
On by default. Agents need your approval every time they save or delete a host or install a public key. You always enter passwords and confirm fingerprints yourself.
Only this device can reach this port.
Some output was dropped by the session limit. Reconnect if the screen is incomplete.
Interactive SSH terminal. Tap to type; swipe vertically to review scrollback.
Private key loaded from the clipboard, and the clipboard was cleared. Save to store it securely on this device.
The host ID must start with a lowercase letter and use only lowercase letters, digits, _ and -, up to 48 characters. Leave it empty and fill in the hostname to generate one.
Another host already uses this ID. Choose a different one.
The ID of a saved host can\'t be changed.
Enter a hostname or IP address without spaces.
The SSH port must be a number from 1 to 65535.
Forwarding ports must be from 1 to 65535, and the target hostname can\'t contain spaces.
Import or paste a private key first, or use Generate key, save and copy public key.
Couldn\'t read the private key file.
The private key is larger than 64 KB. Make sure you chose a private key file.
The clipboard has no text. Copy the whole private key first.
This host has no saved credential. Edit the host to import a key or enter a password.
The host was just changed. Try again.
Only OpenSSH private keys (starting with BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY) are supported. Convert other formats on a computer with ssh-keygen -p -f keyfile.
The private key is invalid or incomplete. Copy the whole key.
This key type or encryption isn\'t supported. Use an Ed25519, ECDSA or RSA key.
Couldn\'t generate a key. Try again.
The server rejected the login. Check the username and password, or make sure the public key is in the server\'s authorized_keys.
Couldn\'t connect. Check the hostname, port and network.
The server refused the connection. Make sure SSH is running on that port.
The host is unreachable. For tailnet hosts, make sure Tailscale is connected and the device is on the allowlist.
The host fingerprint doesn\'t match the saved one. Verify the fingerprint first.
This host\'s fingerprint isn\'t trusted yet. Verify the fingerprint first.
The server\'s host key type isn\'t supported.
Too many connections are open. Close some terminals or forwards first.
Couldn\'t start the foreground service that keeps connections alive.
This host has no port forwarding configured.
SSH is temporarily unavailable. Try again later.
